extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: An open-data supervised fine-tuning reasoning dataset for training reasoning models, built through systematic exploration of a data generation pipeline across math, code, and science. It contains 1.2 million datapoints with 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science examples.
extraction.creator: OpenThoughts project team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built through a multi-stage pipeline that sourced questions from existing math, code, and science sources, filtered questions, deduplicated math and science questions, randomly sampled questions, and generated multiple teacher-model answers per question. Questions from selected sources were expanded or sampled to target sizes, and responses were generated by teacher LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of question sources from existing datasets and corpora across code, math, and science, including StackExchange, OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath, CommonCrawl, FineWeb, organic chemistry textbooks/PDFs, online forums, contests, and chatbot interactions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were generated by teacher/annotator language models rather than human annotators. The pipeline generates multiple answers per question, sweeping 1×, 4×, and 16× answers per question, and selects final strategies by downstream benchmark performance. They also experimented with answer filtering/verification methods but ultimately skipped filtering because it did not outperform using all answers. Teacher models evaluated included DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus, and Claude 3.7 for re-annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was analyzed indirectly through downstream benchmark ablations of teacher choice and filtering/verification strategies. They compared filtering methods and found no-filtering performed similarly to or better than filtered variants; they also compared teacher models and found QwQ-32B outperformed alternatives.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 16 annotations/answers per question in the final pipeline; experiments compared 1×, 4×, and 16×.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Teacher/annotator models DeepSeek-R1, QwQ-32B, Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus, and Claude 3.7 were used for generating/re-annotating answers; a fastText classifier was also used as an answer-filtering tool in code experiments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The work is limited to supervised fine-tuning reasoning data and does not explore reinforcement learning datasets, staged SFT, or curriculum learning. The pipeline choices optimize average benchmark performance rather than domain-specific performance, and assumptions about cross-domain transfer remain uncertain.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The project discusses safety implications of improving open-source reasoning models and aims to ensure models refuse unsafe requests while complying with benign ones.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for supervised fine-tuning/training of reasoning models in math, code, and science, and is released for community use as open-source reasoning data.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The datasets and models are publicly released to the community and available on openthoughts.ai, but no update schedule, maintainer details, or deprecation policy are specified.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Question filtering to select high-quality subsets; deduplication of questions (exact for math and science, none for code); random sampling of questions; generating multiple answers per question with 16× sampling; answer filtering was evaluated but ultimately skipped.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Decontamination against evaluation sets by removing contaminated training samples using normalized Indel similarity and 13-gram overlap; contamination flagged if either method matched, and contaminated samples were discarded.

description.evidence: OpenThoughts3-1.2M, the focus of this paper, is the culmination of the insights gained from the previous OpenThoughts datasets and our systematic exploration... OpenThoughts3-1.2M contains 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "This work has several limitations. We did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning... In each step of our pipeline, we selected strategies that maximized overall average benchmark performance, rather than optimizing for each domain individually... However, it’s unclear whether such transfer persists once domains are mixed."
